title: The Warcraft Movie Took 10 Years and Made Its Money in China
hook: Announced in 2006, released in 2016, and it earned more than four times as much in China as in the US. The Warcraft movie made about 47 million dollars at home and over 200 million in China, enough to be the biggest video game movie ever at the time. Would you watch a Warcraft sequel?
script: Did you know the Warcraft movie took ten years to reach theaters, then earned four times more in China than in America? Blizzard and Legendary Pictures announced the film in May of two thousand six, just before E3. Spider-Man director Sam Raimi signed on in two thousand nine, then left the project three years later. Duncan Jones, the director of Moon, finally took over in two thousand thirteen. Cameras started rolling in Vancouver in January of two thousand fourteen. The movie finally opened in American theaters on June tenth, ten years after that first announcement. American critics were brutal, and it earned only about forty seven million dollars at home. China was a different story. It opened there on a Wednesday and pulled in forty six million dollars in a single day, a record for a weekday opening. Chinese audiences spent more than two hundred million dollars on it in total. Worldwide it finished near four hundred thirty nine million dollars, making it the biggest video game movie ever at the time. Blizzard even gave a free copy of World of Warcraft to Americans who saw it at Regal theaters. And this week Blizzard launched World of Warcraft Forever, a brand new version built around the original two thousand four game. Would you watch a Warcraft sequel? Follow for more gaming history.
